Test Scenario: Post a job with all fields filled correctly
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Fill in every field with valid data 2. Select a company 3. Click Post New Job
Test Data: Title QA Intern, Salary 25000, Location Kathmandu, Position 2
Expected Result: The job is created and the recruiter is taken to the job list, where the new job appears
Actual Result: Result : Sucessfully created job

Test Scenario: Submit the form with every field empty
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Leave all fields blank 2. Click Post New Job
Expected Result: The form is not submitted and a validation message names the fields that are required
Actual Result: Message Displayed: Please fill all the information.
Remarks: Blocked before submission, so the local build does have client-side validation. The message is generic and does not name the missing field, which is recorded as defect JD-05.

Test Scenario: Submit with only the Title filled
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Enter a title only 2. Leave all other fields blank 3. Click Post New Job
Expected Result: The job is not created and the missing fields are identified
Actual Result: Message Displayed: Please fill all the information.

Test Scenario: Check the wording of the validation message
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Leave one field blank 2. Click Post New Job 3. Read the message carefully
Expected Result: The message is spelled correctly and names the field that is missing
Actual Result: Message Displayed: Please fill all the information.
Remarks: Please fill all the information is spelled correctly, but it does not name the field. See JD-05.

Test Scenario: Salary entered as text
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Fill all fields, entering text in Salary 2. Click Post New Job 3. If it saves, open the job list and check what the salary shows as
Expected Result: The entry is rejected, because salary must be a number
Actual Result: Message Displayed: please Enter Valid salary.
Remarks: Rejected correctly. The message begins with a lower case letter while other messages begin with a capital, recorded as defect JD-06.

Test Scenario: Salary entered as a negative number
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Fill all fields, entering -5000 in Salary 2. Click Post New Job
Expected Result: The entry is rejected, because a salary cannot be negative
Actual Result: Message Displayed: please Enter Valid salary.

Test Scenario: Salary entered as zero
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Fill all fields, entering 0 in Salary 2. Click Post New Job
Expected Result: The entry is rejected, or zero is stated to mean unpaid rather than shown as a salary
Actual Result: Result : Sucessfully created job
Remarks: A salary of 0 is accepted while -5000 is rejected, so the check stops at the wrong boundary. Raised as JD-01.

Test Scenario: No of Position entered as zero
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Fill all fields, entering 0 in No of Position 2. Click Post New Job
Expected Result: The entry is rejected, because a job with no openings cannot be posted
Actual Result: Message Displayed : Please Enter valid position.
Remarks: A position of 0 is rejected, while a salary of 0 is accepted. The two fields treat the same boundary differently, which is the point of JD-01.

Test Scenario: No of Position entered as a negative number

Expected Result: The entry is rejected

Test Scenario: No of Position entered as text

Test Scenario: Title containing only spaces

Expected Result: The entry is rejected, because spaces alone are not a title
Actual Result: Message Displayed : Please Enter valid Title.
Remarks: Spaces alone are rejected, so the blank check trims the value first rather than only testing for an empty string.

Test Scenario: Post a job without selecting a company

Test Steps: 1. Fill every field except the company 2. Click Post New Job
Expected Result: The job is not created and the company is identified as required

Test Scenario: Open Post Job with no company registered
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter who has not registered any company
Test Steps: 1. Go to the Post Job page 2. Open the company dropdown 3. Try to post a job
Expected Result: The page explains that a company must be registered first, and does not break
Actual Result: Message Displayed : Please Enter the company name .
Remarks: The page handles an account with no company and shows the same message rather than breaking.

Test Scenario: Post two jobs with identical details
Precondition: Logged in as a Recruiter with at least one company registered, on the Post Job page
Test Steps: 1. Post a job 2. Post a second job with exactly the same details 3. Check the job list
Expected Result: The behaviour is defined, either the duplicate is prevented or both are listed clearly
Actual Result: Result : Sucessfully created job as entered
Remarks: Duplicates are allowed and both postings appear. Not treated as a defect, but worth raising as a product question.

Test Scenario: Job appears on the jobseeker side after posting
Precondition: A job has just been posted by the recruiter
Test Steps: 1. Log out and log in as a Jobseeker 2. Open the job list 3. Find the newly posted job
Expected Result: The job is visible to jobseekers with the correct title, salary and location
Actual Result: Result : Job is visible to sb seeker with correct details
Remarks: Confirms the data reached the database, not only that a success message appeared.
